note: The two title fights are priced about right. The model, the market and the pundits all side with Gane and Harrison, so there's no edge on either winner. The edges I trust are small: (1) Duncan, where the model is far above the line (84% stats-only against 61%) and the matchup backs it: his front-headlock chokes against a 38-year-old who has been stopped three times since 2023, with eight of nine pundits on Duncan. (2) Gane by decision: Hokit has never been stopped and Gane wins by range, not violence, over five rounds. (3) A little more on Radtke at a better price than Thursday's +102. I'm passing on the McKinney-fight round props: the sheet's timing is league-average and ignores that 17 of McKinney's 18 finishes came in R1. Hasan at -1250 is too short, and there's no line yet on Diaz. Total $4 on an $81.71 bankroll, sized well under quarter-Kelly because these edges are thin.

picks.reasoning: Duncan -176. The blended number is 69% against FanDuel's 61%. His choke series (three guillotine or anaconda wins in his four-fight streak) suits Dober's habit of ducking into exchanges. Dober, 38, has three KO/TKO losses since 2023 and is 2-3 in his last five. Dober's left hand is the risk, so half the guide stake.

Gane by decision +390. Our number is 27.5% against FanDuel's 17.7%. Hokit is unbeaten and has never been stopped. Gane wins by distance and footwork, not knockouts of durable men, and the 21 cm reach gap keeps it at range. It's a prop, and my AI Picks pick too, so a small stake.

Radtke +128, adding to Thursday's $1.25 at +102 now the price is better. Thompson is 43, 16 months out after his shin was split to the bone, and lost the grappling in all three recent losses; Radtke's last two wins came from takedowns and control. The favourite is the older man off the long layoff, which fits the underdog check. Small, because the pundits are 8 to 2 on Thompson.
